status_legend.LITERATURE: value or rule taken from a cited paper or standard
status_legend.ESTABLISHED_CONCEPT: follows from standard physics or metrology; reference given
status_legend.ASSUMED: declared for the simulation; no source supports this specific value
status_legend.ENGINEERING_SETTING: a design or threshold choice inside the team's code; not from a paper
status_legend.CONFLICTS_WITH_LITERATURE: used as-is to keep the validated fixture intact, but outside typical published values

sources.SternGeary1957: M. Stern, A.L. Geary, Electrochemical polarization I. A theoretical analysis of the shape of polarization curves, J. Electrochem. Soc. 104(1) (1957) 56-63.
sources.ASTM_G102: ASTM G102-89 (reapproved), Standard Practice for Calculation of Corrosion Rates and Related Information from Electrochemical Measurements. ASTM International.
sources.ASTM_G59: ASTM G59-97 (reapproved), Standard Test Method for Conducting Potentiodynamic Polarization Resistance Measurements. ASTM International.
sources.Mansfeld1976: F. Mansfeld, The polarization resistance technique for measuring corrosion currents, in: Advances in Corrosion Science and Technology, vol. 6, Plenum, 1976, pp. 163-262.
sources.AndradeAlonso2004: C. Andrade, C. Alonso, Test methods for on-site corrosion rate measurement of steel reinforcement in concrete by means of the polarization resistance method (RILEM TC 154-EMC), Materials and Structures 37 (2004) 623-643.
sources.BardFaulkner2001: A.J. Bard, L.R. Faulkner, Electrochemical Methods: Fundamentals and Applications, 2nd ed., Wiley, 2001.
sources.Randles1947: J.E.B. Randles, Kinetics of rapid electrode reactions, Discuss. Faraday Soc. 1 (1947) 11-19.
sources.UNESCO1981: UNESCO, Background papers and supporting data on the Practical Salinity Scale 1978, Technical Papers in Marine Science 37, 1981.
sources.GUM2008: JCGM 100:2008, Evaluation of measurement data - Guide to the expression of uncertainty in measurement (GUM).
sources.ElmerModels: CSC - IT Center for Science, Elmer Models Manual, chapter 'Static Current Conduction' (StatCurrentSolver).
sources.Roache1998: P.J. Roache, Verification and Validation in Computational Science and Engineering, Hermosa Publishers, 1998.
sources.IEC60062: IEC 60062, Marking codes for resistors and capacitors (tolerance code B = 0.1 %).

water.conductivity_S_m.basis: Lies between fresh water (about 0.005-0.05 S/m) and standard seawater (about 5 S/m at 35 salinity, 25 C, from the PSS-78 conductivity ratio). It represents brackish water; no specific water sample was measured.

water.conductivity_relative_half_width.basis: Rectangular half-width converted with u = a/sqrt(3) per GUM 4.3.7; the 1 % magnitude itself is not measured.

steel.exposed_area_m2.basis: 0.02 cm2 face of the validated 40 mm x 50 um planar fixture. Chosen so cell currents stay inside the 1 Mohm TIA range; not a specimen dimension.

electrode_geometry.we_to_ce_gap_m.basis: Validated fixture geometry carried over from configs/physical_integration.json.

electrode_geometry.reference_distance_fr.basis: Mid-gap non-loading RE. Practice places the RE (Luggin tip) close to the WE to reduce Ru; the mid-gap position is a deliberate worst case that makes Ru correction necessary.

geometry_relative_half_widths.basis: Declared rectangular tolerances for width and RE distance.

Ru_model.basis: Ohmic conduction in a uniform planar field. Elmer StatCurrentSolver solves div(sigma grad phi)=0; Ru is extracted from the solved field and checked against the closed form (P4) within 1 %.

elmer.mesh_refinement_check.basis: Solution-verification by systematic mesh refinement; the 1 % gate is the team's engineering setting.

uncertainty_combination.basis: GUM law of propagation for uncorrelated inputs.

cell.Rp_ohm.basis: Gives Rp*A = 2 kohm.cm2 and about 0.15 mm/yr with B = 26 mV, a plausible order for carbon steel in near-neutral water, but no paper gives this value for this system.

cell.Cdl_specific_F_per_cm2.basis: Typical double-layer capacitance of a metal electrode is about 10-40 uF/cm2 (Bard & Faulkner 2001); the upper value is used. Cdl_F = 40 uF/cm2 x 0.02 cm2 = 0.8 uF, giving tau = (Ru*Rp/(Ru+Rp))*Cdl = 7.3 ms. Replaces the earlier 100 uF (5000 uF/cm2), which was about 100x the published range.

cell.model.value: Randles: Ru in series with (Rp || Cdl)
cell.model.basis: Standard equivalent circuit for a corroding electrode without diffusion.

stern_geary_B_V.basis: B = ba*bc/(2.303(ba+bc)). 26 mV corresponds to ba = bc = 120 mV/decade and is the value Andrade and Alonso use for actively corroding steel (52 mV for passive steel). Their context is steel in concrete; it is not measured for this water.

stern_geary_B_range_V.basis: Declared rectangular bound around 26 mV. Published B for steel spans roughly 13-52 mV; a measured Tafel analysis would replace this.

lpr.excitation_amplitudes_V.basis: +-5 mV (A1, A2) and +-10 mV (B) about the open-circuit potential, inside the near-linear region the Stern-Geary approximation needs and inside the +-30 mV window of ASTM G59.

rp_correction.basis: The measured polarization slope includes uncompensated solution resistance, which must be subtracted.

lpr.point_dwell_s.basis: With Cdl = 0.8 uF the first-order cell time constant is tau = (Ru*Rp/(Ru+Rp))*Cdl = 7.3 ms, so the 15 s dwell is far longer than needed for the interface to settle (thousands of tau). The 15 s value itself is P3's engineering setting.

lpr.reacquisition_dwell_s.basis: P3 config: longer observation for a slow transient; one retry maximum.

lpr.sample_rate_hz.basis: Design choice. At 20 Hz the 7.3 ms interface transient is over between samples; the samples measure the settled response, which is what LPR uses.

p3.settling_checks.value: relative slope <= 2 %, window difference <= 5 %, variation <= 25 %, >= 10 s observed
p3.settling_checks.basis: Waiting for a stable potential/current before analysis is standard practice (ASTM G59 requires a stabilisation period). The numerical thresholds are Darshan's engineering settings, not from a paper.

p3.fit_and_signal_thresholds.value: R^2 >= 0.98, SNR >= 10 dB, noise/signal <= 0.25, A1/A2 and A1/B consistency <= 15 %
p3.fit_and_signal_thresholds.basis: Darshan's quality gates; no published source for these exact values.

p3.reference_rule.basis: Known-resistor (dummy cell) check is standard instrument verification practice; the 5 % tolerance is an engineering setting.

instrument.reference_resistor.basis: 0.1 % is a standard precision resistor tolerance class; the resistor is simulated, not a certified standard.

instrument.tia_feedback_ohm.basis: Circuit design value for the nA-uA current range.

corrosion.icorr_model.basis: Stern-Geary relation; assumes uniform corrosion and activation control.
